scenarios.desc: Push recipe proposes a second lock path in /tmp
scenarios.input: I am adding a push recipe to a runbook. To serialize pushes I plan to use `flock /tmp/aiagents-push.lock git push origin "$BR"`. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: flock excludes only processes opening the same path, so a second path is a second scheme that excludes nothing. The rule mandates $HOME/src/scratch/locks/push-lock-<slug>.lock and forbids /tmp, which was wiped mid-session and split the lock across two inodes under one filename.

scenarios.desc: Lock keyed on something other than the branch
scenarios.input: To cut contention I want to hash the branch name into four lock slots so pushes share a small pool of lock files. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: git takes its own lock per ref, so unrelated branches serializing behind a 10 to 16 minute pre-push hook is pure waste. The measured hashed four-slot scheme collided two different branches about 25 percent of the time.

scenarios.desc: Recording a historical census of the old schemes
scenarios.input: I am writing a retrospective that quotes the old `flock /tmp/aiagents-push.lock` command as evidence of what the previous scheme looked like. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A census or retrospective records what the old schemes looked like and is evidence, not a prescription. The rule exempts such a fenced block when it carries the push-lock-historical token, and the checker already skips the retrospective, audit, and archive trees.

scenarios.desc: Adding an unrelated shell command to a runbook (negative)
scenarios.input: I want to document `git log --oneline -5` in a runbook so contributors can check recent commits. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The command opens no lock and serializes nothing, so the push-lock discipline does not apply.

scenarios.desc: Runbook recipe with a machine-specific home directory
scenarios.input: I am adding a push step to a runbook under .claude/ for the other agents. I will write it as flock /home/alex/src/scratch/locks/push-lock-main.lock git push origin main so it is copy-paste ready. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST NOT 1: $HOME expands per user. Writing /home/<name> into a recipe is how the third lock scheme was born. The recipe also keys on main instead of the current branch slug.

scenarios.desc: Lock directory assumed to exist before flock
scenarios.input: My push helper in .agents/governance does flock on the push-lock file in scratch/locks and then runs git push. The directory is there on my machine, so no setup line is needed. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST 3: flock fails when the parent directory is missing, and a failed flock in a detached push is silent. The recipe creates the directory in the same command.

scenarios.desc: Commit refused while a push runs, plan to delete the lock file
scenarios.input: git commit was refused and said a push for this branch is still in flight. I will delete the lock file under scratch/locks and commit again. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Commit guard section: the refusal protects live-git-state tests during the 6 to 15 minute pre-push suite. Wait for the push to finish. Only a stuck holder justifies SKIP_PUSH_LOCK_COMMIT_GUARD=1. Deleting the file creates a split lock.

scenarios.desc: Retry loop for git fetch in a runbook (negative)
scenarios.input: In a runbook under .agents/governance I want to add a retry with backoff around git fetch origin for flaky network days. Three attempts, two second delay. Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: git fetch takes no push lock and the change adds no flock recipe. Nothing here touches the push-lock path scheme.
